presentingComplaint: Left-sided throbbing headache building over the past hour, preceded by 20 minutes of shimmering zig-zag lights in the right visual field.
history: A 29-year-old graphic designer presents to the day-assessment unit 90 minutes into a headache. Twenty minutes before the pain began she noticed a small shimmering, expanding crescent of zig-zag lines (fortification spectrum) drifting across the right half of her vision, which fully resolved over about 20 minutes and was then followed by a gradually intensifying left fronto-temporal throbbing headache. She rates it 5/10 and, atypically for her, has come in early because it started at work. She feels mildly nauseated but has not vomited, dislikes the office lights, and wants to sit in a dim room. Movement makes it worse. She has had 3-4 milder episodes over the last two years, usually perimenstrual (day 1 of her period today) and previously self-managed with ibuprofen and sleep; she has never sought care before. No fever, no neck pain, no recent head injury, no anticoagulants. Mother has 'sick headaches'. On combined oral contraceptive pill. This attack is much less severe and caught far earlier than the fully evolved disabling attacks described in textbooks.
examination: Alert, orientated, comfortable but photophobic, preferring the lights dimmed. No meningism; Kernig and Brudzinski negative. Cranial nerves normal including full visual fields to confrontation and normal fundi with sharp disc margins (no papilloedema). Power, tone, reflexes, coordination and gait all normal. No pronator drift. No temporal artery tenderness. Cardiovascular and general examination unremarkable.
imaging: Not indicated for this typical presentation; non-contrast CT head, if performed to exclude alternatives, is normal.
differentialDiagnoses: Migraine with aura (typical aura with headache)
finalDiagnosis: Migraine with aura, moderate intensity, caught in the early headache phase
citations: International Headache Society - ICHD-3 diagnostic criteria for migraine with aura - 2018
American Headache Society - Acute treatment of migraine in adults - 2021
NICE - Headaches in over 12s: diagnosis and management (CG150) - 2021
contraindications: Combined oral contraceptive is contraindicated in migraine with aura owing to elevated ischaemic stroke risk - switch to a progestogen-only or non-hormonal method
Avoid triptans in uncontrolled hypertension or ischaemic vascular disease
Limit acute analgesic/triptan use to <10-15 days/month to prevent medication-overuse headache
edgeCases: First presentation of aura in an older patient or aura persisting >60 minutes should prompt neuroimaging and stroke/TIA workup
Aura without subsequent headache (acephalgic migraine) can mimic TIA
Sudden maximal (thunderclap) headache is NOT migraine and mandates SAH evaluation
expectedMaiK: Fully reversible visual aura lasting ~20 minutes followed within 60 minutes by unilateral throbbing headache with photophobia and nausea, on a background of recurrent perimenstrual episodes and a normal interval neurological examination, is diagnostic of migraine with aura by ICHD-3; neuroimaging is not required for this typical picture.
expectedNextQuestions: Did the visual symptoms spread gradually and fully resolve, and how long did they last?
Have you had similar attacks before, and are they linked to your periods?
Any weakness, speech difficulty, or symptoms that persisted after the visual disturbance settled?
How many days per month do you take painkillers or other headache medication?
Are you on the combined contraceptive pill or a smoker?
